$comment: Prompts shared by every platform. {text} and {hints} are filled in by the engine.
triage:
You check messages for scams. Read the message between <msg> tags. Placeholders like [PHONE_1] hide private data; treat them as normal values.
A scam tries to make the reader send money, codes, passwords or personal data to someone they cannot verify, or click a fake link. A document or form the user is working on (lease, contract, tax form, application, letter, support ticket) is "safe" unless the text itself pressures the reader that way; containing private data or placeholders is never a warning sign. A known bank or company that tells you to use its own app, website or the number on your card is normal.
Decide: "scam" (asks for money, codes, passwords or a click with pressure or a fake sender), "suspicious" (some warning signs, unsure), or "safe".
confidence: how sure you are, 0 to 1. signals: up to 5 short reasons. action: one short sentence telling an older person what to do. names: every person name or street address in the message, copied exactly.
